I'm repaying Emerald right now and I want to take a nostalgia hike with other Voaters. What's your best memory of Hoenn?

I had a shiny Cacnea. Found it in the desert. I liked it. Evolved it into a Cacturne. Not sure what happened to it, now. I think I traded it to another game so I could restart without losing it. That was my first shiny. I was pleased with it.
I also got my first shiny in Hoenn, It was a tentacool cruising past that haunted island to the berry farm. It's now a nice beefy tentacruel, I raised it even tough it had terrible IV's.

Completely sequence breaking the game by using an Action Replay code to go the island that has Mew on it before the first Gym (it teleported you to the island whenever you walked through a door). I caught the little guy, who was shinyized by another code, with a Master Ball. I then started my journey from the port city with nothing but a underleveled starter and Mewey.

Eventually managed to beat the game by making my way through the Gyms in a completely twisted order because I didn't have Key Items that were needed to work through them normally (HMs and the Devon Scope mainly) and teaching Mewey HMs when I got the badges to use them. It was a fun and unique experience, and I still have Mewey in my game today. I'm thinking about making a run through Alpha Sapphire with Mewey as my starter after next week's Wifi tournament.
I loved the trick house. I always went back to it as soon as I beat a gym. Making the secret bases was a lot of fun too, glad that came back in ORAS.

My best memory of Hoenn is playing with my cousin and competing to see who could finish the game the fastest. We had both already beaten the game many times, so this was just a friendly competition. We were both sitting in the back seat of his mothers car on the way to a Mardi Gras parade, both in front of Kyogre/Groudon frantically throwing Pokeballs trying to be the first to catch them.

Good times.
Well Hoenn region was my first real region I've played. Saphire was my first game, so for me it was choosing my first ever pokemon. Which of course was Mudkip.

This is pretty lame, but when I saw my first Minun. I had seen a Plusle before, but didn't know that Minuns existed until I ran into one. I was a kid and I thought it was so cool that these pokemon were like "twins," and I instantly added them both to my party. Even now I ALWAYS have a Minun in my party and it quickly became my favorite pokemon, overtaking Nidoking. I know he's not the strongest or fastest, but he is just so cheerful it gives me the "courage" to keep going in the game. Fun times :)

New voater here! Took a crack at customizing this beast (the entire site, not just a single subaverse)! Need feedback on my userstyle.

Here are my thoughts:

  • The comment box is small.
  • The horizontal rules cut under the sidebar.
  • The header holds an inconsistent look with the rest of the site.
  • The interface is the anti-Christ of tablet and other touch-based users.
  • The site has no outside margins at all, which looks really weird. Even the anarchists use at least 10 pixels left and right.
  • Comment and post readability is complete chaos. There is no max width and no line height to compensate. Even Reddit limits their comment lines so it's readable.
  • The preview pane does not act as intended.
  • The settings page is broken.

So you're aware, I realized halfway into writing this comment that I was supposed to use night mode. I edited my points to reflect this, but, as they remain now, they are valid.

All in all, the user style appears to have no theme (other than my night mode theme). The controls are way too close together for touch-based usability. The margins, paddings, and widths are chaotic, which breaks a lot of controls throughout the site as well as putting a strain on readability. Many well-accepted web design standards have been tossed out to 'weed' out 'unnecessary' styles set in the site design.

I think, perhaps, you should start with a single subverse theme and work your way up to entire site status.

If I sound too harsh, it's because you've made your theme publicly available, meaning that some of my points warn subverse owners my reasons why it might be a bad idea to adopt it into their subs. But it is also there to give you insight from my experiences designing Voat. Of course, I am happy to find those like you who take an interest in CSS! Good luck.

  • Comment and post readability is complete chaos. There is no max width and no line height to compensate. Even Reddit limits their comment lines so it's readable.

    • Fixed
